new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (25 pp., text layer, Language in Africa 1(3) 100-124, open PDF from iling-ran.ru). Both quoted passages are there verbatim: p. 104 (PDF p. 5, end of §2 'The Bena-Yungur tone system'): "The internal reconstruction of an original two-tone system is confirmed by the fact that Bena-Yungur's closest relatives Mboi and Laala-Roba have a two-way tonal opposition as well, at least in our current analysis."; p. 101 (§1 Introduction): "Where relevant and possible, we will adduce new external evidence from the ongoing documentation of the related languages Laala-Roba [Glottocode: lala1261] and Mboi [Glottocode: mboi1246]." Only differences are line breaks. Read §1-§2 and the comparanda in (23)…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Lala-Roba is a tone language with a two-way (H vs L) lexical tonal opposition, per the authors' own ongoing field documentation (LLACAN). No source opened says anything about word stress, its position, or its absence; the tone-marked wordlists of Kleinewillinghöfer (Laala of Bodwai, Laala of Yang, Roba) are consistent with a two-tone language but carry no prose.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the tonal statement is hedged ('at least in our current analysis').
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on word stems (nouns and verbs, e.g. nàm-ó 'meat', fə̀tá(ː) 'horn', tòmó 'do', káwà 'break'); no statement about phrase-level prosody or citation forms. Variety not specified beyond 'Laala-Roba'; the 2019 classification slides cite 'Laala of Yang'.
new_statements.identity_note: Idiatov & Van de Velde 2020 name the language 'Laala-Roba [Glottocode: lala1261]' explicitly, so the tone statement covers the Glottolog language as a whole; their comparanda are not assigned to a dialect (the 2019 slides cite 'Laala of Yang' once). Kleinewillinghöfer's data distinguish Ɓəna Laala of Bodwai (Bodei), Ɓəna Laala of Yang, and Robma/Roba (roba1240); Ishaku 2023 names dialects Roɓa, Ɓəna, Sĩĩri. Idiatov (2023) now calls the Bena-Mboi group 'Buto'. Not to be confused with Ɓəna-Yungur (bena1260, ISO yun), the sister language that the 2018/2020 papers actually describe.

sources.locator: p. 104, §2 'The Bena-Yungur tone system' (end of section); Laala-Roba data source stated p. 101, §1
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the paper. §2 describes the Bena-Yungur tone system (3 level tones, no downstep); p. 104 states that Bena-Yungur's closest relatives Mboi and Laala-Roba have a two-way tonal opposition 'at least in our current analysis'; p. 101 says the Laala-Roba data come from the authors' ongoing documentation; tone-marked Laala-Roba comparanda in (23), (24), (36).
